qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Deep B2B2C integration into telecom carrier billing systems (e.g. T-Mobile), auto dealer networks, and mortgage servicer tracking platforms creates substantial partner switching costs. 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 24.8% demonstrates strong fee-based capital efficiency and pricing power to offset repair and replacement cost inflation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). While Assurant possesses a verified switching-cost moat in B2B2C specialty warranty administration and mortgage tracking with a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 24.8%, its competitive runway fails the 15-year persistence standard. Connected Living (over 50% of revenue) suffers from acute client concentration with T-Mobile, exposing the business to contract re-bidding, fee-split compression, or OEM disintermediation (AppleCare+ direct expansion). In addition, Global Housing property underwriting faces structural climate headwinds and rising catastrophe reinsurance costs that periodically disrupt earnings. Under Munger default-reject, a contract-dependent warranty administrator cannot support a 15+ year CAP.
qualitative.evidence: FY2025 revenue reached $12.8B ($10.55B US, $2.27B international) and EBIT reached $1,197M with GAAP ROIC of 26.2% and 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 24.8%. Free cash flow conversion is strong at 1.10x. However, historical earnings show significant volatility driven by catastrophe losses and underwriting cycles (net income dropped to $251M in FY2018 and $277M in FY2022 with GAAP ROIC dipping to 6.4% and 11.9%). Global Lifestyle accounts for the majority of revenue, heavily concentrated in Connected Living mobile device protection tied to carrier partnerships (primarily T-Mobile), leaving the economic engine vulnerable to partner contract renegotiation and direct OEM warranty competition over a multi-decade horizon.
